title: Keyboard access and focus order
learningObjectives: Explain keyboard access and focus order and apply inclusive semantic HTML practices.

understand.concept: Keyboard accessibility ensures interactive controls can be reached and operated without a pointer. Native links, buttons, and form controls have expected keyboard behaviour. Focus order should follow a logical reading and interaction sequence, and focus indicators must remain visible.
understand.whyItMatters: Some users rely on keyboards, switch devices, or alternative input. Removing outlines, using positive tabindex values, or making non-semantic clickable divs can create barriers.
understand.analogy: Keyboard focus is the user's place in the interface; it should move through controls in a predictable order.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; accessibility APIs, semantics, and assistive technology behaviour require standards-based implementation and testing.

explain.narrative: The skip link moves users to main content. Native controls participate in keyboard navigation and focus styling remains visible.

practise.guidedTask: Navigate a sample page using Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, and Space. Fix any unexpected focus order or invisible focus indicator.
practise.independentTask: Audit a small page using keyboard navigation and an accessibility tree. Fix semantics, labels, alternatives, and relationships without adding unnecessary ARIA.
hints: Use native HTML where it provides the required semantics.
Keep visible labels and focus indicators.
Test meaningful content with keyboard and assistive technology where available.
